dimensions.name: Discovery & Crawlability

findings.finding: Trailing-slash and /sitemap.xml redirects downgrade the scheme to plain HTTP.
findings.evidence: GET https://kin.rag.wtf/about -> 301 Location: http://kin.rag.wtf/about/; GET https://kin.rag.wtf/sitemap.xml -> 301 Location: http://kin.rag.wtf/sitemap-index.xml. nginx listens on :80 behind Cloudflare TLS and emits absolute redirects with its own scheme.
findings.remediation: Add `absolute_redirect off;` to the nginx server block (or build Location from $http_x_forwarded_proto) so redirects stay relative / HTTPS.
findings.impact: Removes an extra hop and an insecure intermediate URL for every crawler that follows a non-canonical link; strict agents that refuse HTTP downgrades stop failing.

findings.finding: The MCP manifest at /.well-known/mcp.json is not referenced from any discovery file.
findings.evidence: robots.txt agent-discovery comments and the llms.txt 'Technical' section list llms.txt, llms-full.txt, portfolio.json, openapi.json, ai-plugin.json, agent.json and agent-policy, but not /.well-known/mcp.json (which returns 200).
findings.remediation: Add the MCP manifest (or, once one exists, the MCP server URL) to robots.txt comments, the llms.txt Technical section and ai-plugin.json.
findings.impact: Agents that discover from llms.txt or robots.txt alone find every agent surface.

findings.finding: Every sitemap <lastmod> is the build timestamp, not the content change date.
findings.evidence: All 28 <url> entries in /sitemap-0.xml carry <lastmod>2026-10-19T07:43:44.371Z</lastmod> and <changefreq>weekly</changefreq>.
findings.remediation: Feed per-page dates into @astrojs/sitemap `serialize` (article publishDate, project dateStarted / file mtime) and drop lastmod for pages without a real date.
findings.impact: Crawlers and retrieval agents can skip unchanged pages instead of re-fetching the whole site after every deploy.

findings.finding: /.well-known/agent-policy and /site.webmanifest are served as application/octet-stream.
findings.evidence: curl -w '%{content_type}' -> application/octet-stream for both; the policy is Markdown-style text and the manifest is JSON.
findings.remediation: Add nginx `location = /.well-known/agent-policy { default_type text/plain; }` and map .webmanifest to application/manifest+json.
findings.impact: Fetch tools that skip binary content types will read the policy instead of discarding it.

strengths: Complete discovery stack: robots.txt (Allow: /, sitemap reference, commented agent-discovery block), sitemap-index.xml (28 URLs), llms.txt, llms-full.txt (27 KB), ai-plugin.json at root and /.well-known/, RSS at /rss.xml (linked via <link rel=alternate>), /.well-known/agent-policy and security.txt.
robots.txt does not block any agent; GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot and Google-Extended all receive HTTP 200 with byte-identical HTML.
URL topology is flat and predictable: /projects/<slug>/, /insights/<slug>/, trailing slash enforced.
dimensions.summary: Near-complete discovery stack including feed and agent policy. Only hygiene issues remain: HTTP-downgrading redirects, build-time lastmod values, the MCP manifest missing from the indexes, and two files with a binary content type.

dimensions.name: Machine Readability

findings.finding: Raw text-to-HTML ratio is low because of utility-class markup and serialized island props, although all meaningful text is server-rendered.
findings.evidence: Home page: 4,223 visible text chars in 84,220 bytes of HTML (5.0%), with 15,442 bytes of inline script and 10 <astro-island> elements carrying JSON props. Project detail pages sit at 5-6%.
findings.remediation: Optional: offer per-page Markdown alternates (e.g. /projects/claim-pilot/index.md) linked with <link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">, so token-constrained agents need not parse the HTML.
findings.impact: Cuts the tokens an agent spends per page by roughly an order of magnitude.

strengths: Astro static build: every heading, project description, career entry, article summary and form label is present in the initial HTML with JavaScript disabled.
The only client-only island is the decorative DotGrid canvas (client:only); every other island hydrates over server-rendered markup.
No console errors on load (checked in Chrome).
dimensions.summary: Static site generation with complete server-rendered content. The low raw ratio is markup overhead, not missing content.

dimensions.name: Semantic Structure

findings.finding: Numbered section headings extract as run-together text ("01Selected Work").
findings.evidence: Home h2.innerHTML = '01Selected Work'; textContent = '01Selected Work', '02Career', '03Latest Writing'. The spacing is visual (margin) only.
findings.remediation: Mark the number aria-hidden="true" and put a real space or separator after it, or move the number into a ::before pseudo-element.
findings.impact: Clean heading text in DOM-to-text extraction and in screen-reader heading lists.

findings.finding: A navigation link is marked up as a heading, and external-link hints pollute heading text.
findings.evidence:
Home:

All projects →

inside the Work track. About: h3 text reads e.g. 'Senior Java Tech Lead @ DXC Technology (opens in a new tab)' because the sr-only hint sits inside the heading's link.
findings.remediation: Render 'All projects' as a plain link (not h3). Move the company link and its '(opens in a new tab)' hint outside the h3, or use aria-describedby for the hint.
findings.impact: Heading outline reflects document structure; extracted job titles are clean.

findings.finding: Home 'Latest Writing' items have no per-article headings.
findings.evidence: Home heading outline goes h2 '03Latest Writing' -> h2 'Have a workflow that should run itself?' with no h3 for the three article rows; /insights/ uses h2 per article.
findings.remediation: Give ArticleRow a heading level prop and render titles as h3 on the home page.
findings.impact: Agents navigating by heading can reach each article from the home page.

strengths: Landmarks on every page: <header>, aria-labelled <nav> ('Main navigation', 'Mobile navigation', 'Footer links', breadcrumb), single <main id=main-content>, <footer>; skip link present.
One h1 per page; inner pages have clean h1 -> h2 -> h3 outlines.
Interactive controls are native <button>/<a>: menu toggle has aria-expanded + aria-controls='mobile-nav'; console pause button has an aria-label; the closed drawer is inert.
All contact-form inputs have <label for> associations and aria-describedby error slots; html lang='en'.
dimensions.summary: Strong landmark and control semantics. Deductions are for heading text quality: run-together section numbers, a link styled as h3, and link hints inside headings.

dimensions.name: Content Extraction Friendliness

findings.finding: JSON-LD entities are not linked with @id; the Person is re-declared inline in every block.
findings.evidence: 0 occurrences of "@id" across 8 pages checked. Home has 5 JSON-LD blocks with 'Person' declared 8 times (once in full, then as author of each SoftwareApplication/SoftwareSourceCode).
findings.remediation: Give the Person and WebSite stable ids (https://kin.rag.wtf/#person, /#website) and reference them via {"@id": ...} from author, publisher and about properties; consider a single @graph per page.
findings.impact: Knowledge-graph consumers merge every mention into one entity instead of many anonymous Persons.

findings.finding: Article schema on /insights/<slug>/ points url to Medium and keeps speakable in a separate WebPage block.
findings.evidence: Zero-trust page: Article.url = https://limcheekin.medium.com/...; no mainEntityOfPage, no dateModified; speakable lives on a sibling WebPage block (selectors #article-title and .prose-like both exist in the DOM).
findings.remediation: Add mainEntityOfPage (the on-site URL), keep url or add sameAs for the Medium original, add dateModified, and attach speakable to the WebPage that has mainEntity = the Article.
findings.impact: Disambiguates the on-site summary from the canonical Medium article and ties the speakable region to the entity it describes.

findings.finding: The JSON API omits experience descriptions that exist in the content collection.
findings.evidence: /api/portfolio.json and /api/experience.json experience objects only contain company, title, startDate, endDate, technologies. llms-full.txt and /about/ carry the description bullets for the same entries.
findings.remediation: Export `description` (array of strings) per experience entry in scripts/generate-api.ts and add it to the Experience schema in openapi.json.
findings.impact: Agents that use the structured API (the advertised primary path) get responsibilities and outcomes, not just job titles.

findings.finding: All pages share one og:image.
findings.evidence: og:image = https://kin.rag.wtf/images/portfolio.png on home, about, projects, every project and article page and the 404.
findings.remediation: Use the project screenshot as og:image where a project has one; generate simple title cards for articles.
findings.impact: Link-preview and multimodal agents can tell pages apart.

strengths: JSON-LD on 100% of pages checked (8/8 plus 404), all parse cleanly.

Rich, page-appropriate types: Person (jobTitle, knowsAbout, sameAs, worksFor), WebSite with ReadAction, FAQPage (10 Q&A), ItemList of SoftwareApplication / SoftwareSourceCode, ItemList of Article, ContactPage, BreadcrumbList on every inner page.
speakable (SpeakableSpecification) present on article pages, with selectors that resolve in the DOM.
Machine-readable mirrors: /api/portfolio.json (13 projects, 10 articles, 11 roles) and llms-full.txt.
dimensions.summary: Excellent structured-data coverage. Improvements are refinements: entity @id linking, article main-entity disambiguation, and bringing the JSON API up to parity with llms-full.txt.

dimensions.name: DOM Stability & Selector Robustness

findings.finding: data-testid coverage stops at chrome and the contact form; repeated content items have none.
findings.evidence: Home exposes 13 testids (logo-link, nav-link-*, hero-cta, mobile-menu-toggle, main-content...). /projects/ and /insights/ expose 10 each, all site chrome: project cards, article rows, career entries and breadcrumb items have no data-testid.
findings.remediation: Add data-testid="project-card" + data-slug on ProjectCard, "article-row" + data-slug on ArticleRow, "career-entry" on timeline items.
findings.impact: Browser agents and tests can target a specific project or article by slug without relying on text or Tailwind class chains.

strengths: Contact form fully instrumented: contact-form, contact-field-name/email/message, contact-form-submit, contact-form-success.
Stable semantic ids: #main-content, #mobile-nav, #contact-name, #contact-email, #contact-message, #article-title.
Tailwind utility classes are stable across builds; no CSS-module hashing in the DOM (only bundle filenames are hashed).
dimensions.summary: Stable selectors for navigation and the form; content collections would benefit from slug-keyed test ids.

dimensions.name: Navigation Clarity & Task Discoverability

findings.finding: No GET-based search; the only search is a WebMCP tool that most agents cannot reach.
findings.evidence: No search form or ?q= route exists. WebMCPTools registers search_portfolio only when navigator.modelContext exists; in Chrome without WebMCP support navigator.modelContext is undefined and nothing registers.
findings.remediation: For a site of 28 URLs this is acceptable; optionally publish a small static search index (/api/search.json with title, slug, tags, summary) and reference it in llms.txt and openapi.json.
findings.impact: Gives non-WebMCP agents a documented way to locate content by keyword.

findings.finding: Visible navigation labels differ from URL segments.
findings.evidence: Nav label 'Work' -> /projects/, 'Writing' -> /insights/ (data-testid nav-link-work, nav-link-writing). Breadcrumbs say 'Projects' and 'Writing'.
findings.remediation: Keep the URLs (they are stable), but align the label with the breadcrumb ('Projects') or add aria-describedby/title so label and destination agree; mention the mapping in llms.txt.
findings.impact: Agents inferring paths from labels (e.g. guessing /work/ or /writing/) land correctly.

strengths: All navigation is real <a href> links (0 JS-only links across 8 pages); nav is labelled and present identically in header, mobile drawer and footer.
Descriptive hierarchical URLs: /projects/project-concord/, /insights/zero-trust-ai-agents/.
Visual breadcrumbs plus BreadcrumbList JSON-LD on every inner page.
Custom 404 offers Home, Projects, Writing and Contact links.
dimensions.summary: Clear, predictable navigation with breadcrumbs. Small gaps: no GET search and label/URL naming mismatch.

dimensions.name: Form & Workflow Design

findings.finding: Post-submit redirect relies on a relative `_next` value at a third-party endpoint.
findings.evidence: <input type=hidden name=_next value="/contact/?submitted=true">; form action=https://formspree.io/f/xzdyblya. Formspree's documented `_next` expects an absolute URL; the success panel (#contact-success, role=status) only appears when ?submitted=true is present. Not verified by submission (passive audit).
findings.remediation: Use an absolute value (https://kin.rag.wtf/contact/?submitted=true), confirm the Formspree plan honours custom redirects, or submit with fetch() and Accept: application/json and render the result inline.
findings.impact: Guarantees the visitor (or a supervised agent) returns to an on-site, machine-readable confirmation instead of a third-party page.

findings.finding: Form uses `novalidate`; constraint feedback depends on client JavaScript.
findings.evidence: <form ... novalidate>; inline messages are written by a script on the 'invalid' event. Without JS the browser shows no hints and validation falls to Formspree.
findings.remediation: Acceptable trade-off (documented in a source comment). Optionally add a static hint (e.g. 'At least 10 characters') to each field's describedby text so constraints are readable without JS.
findings.impact: Constraints become visible to agents that read the DOM without executing scripts.

strengths: Every visible input has a <label for>, a typed control (type=text, type=email, textarea), name, required, and autocomplete (name, email).
HTML5 constraints present: minlength=2 + pattern='.{2,}' on name, minlength=10 on message.
Explicit action and method=POST; aria-describedby points at per-field error elements; submit button is a native <button type=submit> with a testid.
Agent policy states the form is for human use and email is published in llms.txt, portfolio.json and the footer, giving agents a sanctioned alternative.
dimensions.summary: Well-structured single-step form. The open question is the third-party redirect back to the on-site confirmation.

dimensions.name: Error Handling & Recovery

findings.finding: Unknown /api/ paths return the HTML 404 page instead of a JSON error.
findings.evidence: GET https://kin.rag.wtf/api/nope.json -> 404 text/html (the full site 404 page with island markup).
findings.remediation: In nginx `location /api/` add `error_page 404 = @api404;` and `location @api404 { default_type application/json; return 404 '{"error":"not_found","docs":"/api/openapi.json"}'; }`. Declare a 404 response in openapi.json.
findings.impact: API clients get a parseable error that points back to the spec.

findings.finding: Error-field linkage uses aria-describedby only; no aria-errormessage, and the 404 page declares a canonical URL.
findings.evidence: Fields get aria-invalid=true plus aria-describedby='contact-*-error' (works). 404.html has <link rel=canonical href=https://kin.rag.wtf/404/> and is served for every missing path.
findings.remediation: Optionally add aria-errormessage alongside aria-describedby. Drop the canonical (or add noindex) on the 404 template.
findings.impact: Prevents indexers associating every missing URL with /404/.

strengths: Missing pages return a true HTTP 404 with a helpful page (heading, explanation, four recovery links), not a soft 200.
Inline, persistent field errors with specific fix-it messages ('Enter a valid email address, like name@example.com'); focus moves to the first invalid field.
Conditional GET works: If-None-Match with the current ETag returns 304.
dimensions.summary: Good human-facing recovery. API errors are HTML, which is the main gap for agents.

dimensions.name: Authentication & Session Handling
strengths: No task on the site requires authentication; all pages, the API and the agent files are public.
Auth model declared accurately and consistently: ai-plugin.json auth.type='none', agent.json authentication.type='none'.
CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on /api/ allows browser-based agents to fetch data cross-origin.
dimensions.summary: Not applicable in the usual sense: a public read-only site with the 'no auth' model declared in machine-readable manifests. No barrier for agents.

dimensions.name: Anti-Bot Friction

findings.finding: Contact submissions go through a third-party processor that may interpose a challenge.
findings.evidence: Form posts to formspree.io. Formspree can apply reCAPTCHA to plain HTML submissions depending on form settings; not verified because the audit does not submit forms. The agent policy prohibits automated form submission anyway.
findings.remediation: No action needed for agents (email is the sanctioned path). If human friction matters, review the Formspree reCAPTCHA setting.
findings.impact: Documents the only possible friction point; it does not affect any read task.

strengths: Cloudflare fronts the site but serves no challenge: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, python-requests and curl all get HTTP 200 with byte-identical HTML.
No CAPTCHA on any read workflow.
Advisory rate limits are documented in headers (X-RateLimit-Limit: 60, X-RateLimit-Policy: 60;w=60) and in /.well-known/agent-policy.
dimensions.summary: Agent-friendly: no bot challenges, documented courtesy limits. The only theoretical friction is on a form agents are asked not to submit.

dimensions.name: API/Tool Exposure

findings.finding: OpenAPI spec under-describes the actual responses.
findings.evidence: openapi.json 3.0.3 declares only 200 responses (no 404/304), and the Experience schema omits description while the Project schema omits githubUrl/liveUrl requirements per kind and the stack field. No ETag/Cache-Control headers documented.
findings.remediation: Generate openapi.json from the same types as generate-api.ts, add 304/404 responses and response headers (ETag, Cache-Control, X-RateLimit-*), and mark required properties.
findings.impact: Code-generating agents get accurate types and know they can poll conditionally.

strengths: OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec with 6 documented paths; all resolve with HTTP 200 (portfolio.json, projects.json, experience.json, articles.json, llms.txt, llms-full.txt).
Polling-friendly: Cache-Control 'public, max-age=3600, must-revalidate', weak ETag, Last-Modified, and verified 304 on If-None-Match.
Spec is referenced from llms.txt, ai-plugin.json (api.type='openapi') and robots.txt comments.
Client-side WebMCP tools (get_projects, get_experience, get_contact_info, search_portfolio) registered when navigator.modelContext is present.
dimensions.summary: Strong static API surface for a portfolio, with caching semantics agents can exploit. Spec fidelity is the remaining improvement.

dimensions.name: Observability & Outcome Verification

findings.finding: The on-site submission confirmation depends on the third-party redirect working.
findings.evidence: contact.astro reveals #contact-success (role=status, aria-live=polite, data-testid=contact-form-success) only when location.search includes 'submitted=true'; see T2 for the _next concern.
findings.remediation: Same fix as T2; with a fetch() submission, render success or the Formspree error JSON into the live region.
findings.impact: One deterministic, persistent success indicator in the DOM and URL.

strengths: Persistent success region with role=status and a stable testid, plus URL state (?submitted=true).
API responses carry metadata.generatedAt and version, plus Last-Modified and ETag, so agents can verify freshness.
Submit button changes to 'Sending…' and is disabled during submission, preventing duplicate posts.
dimensions.summary: Read-only site with good freshness signals; the single write path has a clear DOM confirmation pattern.

dimensions.name: Content Consistency & Determinism
strengths: Identical HTML (same MD5) served to iPhone Safari, desktop Chrome, GPTBot and ClaudeBot user agents: no UA sniffing, no A/B variants.
Responsive behaviour is CSS and progressive enhancement only; the Work track uses the same DOM for the pinned desktop and swipe mobile layouts.
Animated hero console content is aria-hidden and decorative; the meaningful copy is static.
dimensions.summary: Fully deterministic static output across user agents and viewports.

dimensions.name: GEO Alignment

findings.finding: Home meta description has a grammar error.
findings.evidence: <meta name=description content="Personal portfolio for Lim Chee Kin, a AI Solutions Architect, ...">
findings.remediation: Change to 'an AI Solutions Architect' (or rewrite as a concrete one-sentence value statement matching llms.txt).
findings.impact: The most-quoted snippet of the site reads correctly in AI overviews and search results.

findings.finding: Article pages are short summaries; the citable body lives on Medium.
findings.evidence: /insights/zero-trust-ai-agents/ has 825 visible chars of text; Article.url and the main link point to limcheekin.medium.com.
findings.remediation: Add a 'Key points' list (3-5 quotable bullets) to each insight page so generative engines can cite the portfolio directly.
findings.impact: More on-site citation-ready content per topic.

strengths: FAQPage with 10 question/answer pairs on the home page.
Clear entity declarations: Person with jobTitle, worksFor, knowsAbout, sameAs; llms.txt opens with a one-line definition of who the site is about.
Project and career copy is concise and outcome-oriented, easy to quote.
dimensions.summary: Well optimised for generative extraction; small copy fixes and richer on-site article summaries would complete it.

dimensions.name: A2A Readiness

findings.finding: Agent card describes a website, not an A2A service endpoint, and uses non-current field names.
findings.evidence: /.well-known/agent.json: url='https://kin.rag.wtf' (static site, does not accept A2A JSON-RPC), 'schema_version' instead of 'protocolVersion', no 'provider' or 'documentationUrl'. /.well-known/agent-card.json (path used by current A2A versions) -> 404.
findings.remediation: Add protocolVersion, provider {organization, url}, documentationUrl (llms.txt); also publish the card at /.well-known/agent-card.json. Either describe skills as 'read static resources' with explicit resource URLs, or stand up a minimal A2A endpoint.
findings.impact: A2A orchestrators that validate against the current schema accept the card and do not attempt JSON-RPC calls against the site root.

strengths: Agent card present (HTTP 200, valid JSON) with name, description, version, capabilities, authentication (type none), input/output modes and two skills.
Linked from robots.txt comments and the llms.txt Technical section.
dimensions.summary: Valid, discoverable card with accurate auth; capability and endpoint declarations are thin relative to the A2A spec.

dimensions.name: MCP Server Readiness

findings.finding: No working MCP server: /.well-known/mcp.json is a static resource list without a transport endpoint.
findings.evidence: /.well-known/mcp.json lists three HTTPS resources (portfolio.json, llms-full.txt, llms.txt) with mcpVersion '1.0' but no server URL or transport; POST initialize to it -> 405 text/html. No MCP URL in llms.txt, ai-plugin.json or openapi.json servers.
findings.remediation: Deploy a small read-only MCP server (Streamable HTTP, e.g. /mcp via a Cloudflare Worker) exposing resources for projects, experience and articles and tools mirroring the WebMCP set (get_projects, get_experience, search_portfolio). Document its URL in llms.txt, ai-plugin.json, mcp.json and robots.txt.
findings.impact: Claude and other MCP clients can connect directly, and it would demonstrate the owner's own MCP expertise on the portfolio itself.

strengths: A manifest exists and correctly lists the machine-readable resources.
Equivalent tools already exist client-side via WebMCP (four tools), so the tool design is done.
dimensions.summary: MCP intent is visible but there is no reachable server. Highest-leverage remaining differentiator for a site about agentic AI.

task_profiles.evidence: robots.txt, sitemap-index.xml (28 URLs incl. every project and article), llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai-plugin.json, agent.json, agent-policy and rss.xml all return 200 and cross-reference each other.
task_profiles.notes: Redirects to http:// on non-canonical URLs and the unlisted mcp.json are hygiene issues, not blockers.

task_profiles.evidence: <nav aria-label='Main navigation'> with plain <a href> to /about/, /projects/, /insights/, /contact/, /resume.pdf; BreadcrumbList on every inner page; 0 JS-only links.
Person, WebSite, FAQPage, ItemList, SoftwareApplication/SoftwareSourceCode, Article (+speakable), ContactPage and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD; /api/portfolio.json with 13 projects, 10 articles, 11 roles.
task_profiles.notes: API experience entries lack description text present in llms-full.txt.

task_profiles.evidence: Contact form: 3/3 visible inputs labelled via for/id, typed (text/email/textarea), required, minlength, autocomplete, explicit POST action. Email published as a sanctioned alternative.
task_profiles.notes: Not submitted (passive audit). Agent policy reserves the form for humans; the relative _next redirect should be verified.

task_profiles.evidence: HTML pages: true 404 status with recovery links; inline field errors linked via aria-describedby. API: /api/nope.json returns the HTML 404 page, no JSON error body.
task_profiles.notes: Add a JSON 404 under /api/ and document error responses in OpenAPI.

immediate.action: Set `absolute_redirect off;` in nginx so trailing-slash and /sitemap.xml redirects stay on HTTPS.
immediate.impact: Removes HTTP-downgrade hop for every non-canonical URL.

immediate.action: Fix nginx add_header inheritance: repeat the security headers (or use an include) in the /api/ and .html locations; HTML currently ships without X-Frame-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
immediate.impact: Restores the intended security headers on pages and API responses.

immediate.action: Return a JSON 404 body for unknown /api/ paths and declare it in openapi.json.
Export experience `description` in generate-api.ts and the OpenAPI Experience schema.
immediate.impact: Structured API reaches parity with llms-full.txt.

immediate.action: Make the Formspree `_next` value absolute (or switch to a fetch() JSON submission) and verify the on-site confirmation appears.
Fix 'a AI Solutions Architect' in the home meta description.

short_term.action: Add @id-linked entities (/#person, /#website) across all JSON-LD; add mainEntityOfPage and dateModified to Article.
Clean heading text: aria-hidden section numbers with a real separator, 'All projects' as a link, link hints outside About h3s, h3 titles in home Latest Writing.
Update agent.json to current A2A fields (protocolVersion, provider, documentationUrl) and also serve it at /.well-known/agent-card.json.
short_term.impact: Card validates against current A2A schema.

short_term.action: Reference /.well-known/mcp.json from llms.txt and robots.txt; serve agent-policy as text/plain and the webmanifest as application/manifest+json.
short_term.impact: Every agent surface discoverable from the indexes.

short_term.action: Use real per-page lastmod dates in the sitemap.
Add slug-keyed data-testid to ProjectCard, ArticleRow and career entries.

medium_term.action: Deploy a read-only MCP server (Streamable HTTP) mirroring the WebMCP tools and API resources; document it in llms.txt, ai-plugin.json and mcp.json.
medium_term.impact: Direct MCP integration; largest remaining protocol gain.

medium_term.action: Publish per-page Markdown alternates and a small /api/search.json index.
medium_term.impact: Lower token cost per page; keyword lookup for non-WebMCP agents.

medium_term.action: Add 3-5 quotable key points to each /insights/ page and per-page og:image cards.

robots_txt.content_summary: User-agent: * / Allow: /; Sitemap: https://kin.rag.wtf/sitemap-index.xml; commented 'Agent discovery' block listing llms.txt, llms-full.txt, portfolio.json, ai-plugin.json, agent.json and agent-policy.

sitemap_xml.content_summary: /sitemap.xml 301-redirects (via http://) to /sitemap-index.xml -> /sitemap-0.xml with 28 URLs (home, about, contact, /projects/ + 13 projects, /insights/ + 10 articles). All lastmod values equal the build time.

llms_txt.content_summary: 6 KB Markdown index: summary line, About, Core Skills, Current Projects (enterprise + open source), Past Contributions, Work Experience, Articles (Medium links), Contact, Technical links to every agent surface except mcp.json. llms-full.txt (27 KB) has full project bodies and career bullets.

schema_org.quality_assessment: Rich and valid on every page type (all blocks parse). Missing @id entity linking and mainEntityOfPage on articles.

ai_plugin_json.content_summary: Served at /ai-plugin.json and /.well-known/ai-plugin.json (identical). auth none, api.type openapi -> /api/openapi.json.

agent_json.content_summary: A2A-style card with name, description, version 1.0, capabilities (all false), authentication none, two skills. /.well-known/agent-card.json returns 404.

mcp_json.content_summary: Static manifest listing three HTTPS resources; no server endpoint or transport.

emerging_standards_readiness.notes: nlweb_mcp_ready: complete JSON-LD on all page types plus a JSON API makes the content ready for conversational querying. webmcp_ready: WebMCPTools.tsx registers get_projects, get_experience, get_contact_info and search_portfolio through navigator.modelContext.registerTool when the API exists (feature-detected, no polyfill; inactive in the Chrome build used for this audit). voix_ready: no Voix markup.
